topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation-driven cancer development and susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutation accumulation can produce cancer when cellular susceptibility and the surrounding environment permit clonal evolution.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and interpretation of causal evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about environmental exposures informs the balance between avoidable cancer risks and apparently chance events.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the argument through a detailed example.

topics.label: Environmental DNA damage and carcinogen activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures generate mutation-producing DNA damage and how cellular metabolism can determine their carcinogenic activity.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Biological context of carcinogen susceptibility and synthesis of mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of carcinogenic mechanisms by showing how the biological context of exposure shapes susceptibility.

topics.label: Evidence linking human cancers to carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how observations from human populations and biological samples can connect cancer development to particular exposures.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess how experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions around the risk–benefit judgments involved in carcinogen exposure.
